merger_description:
Tasman Tourism Pty Ltd, as trustee for the Tasman Tourism Trust (**Tasman Tourism**) proposes to acquire the business and assets of the Trustee for Amberlee Family Trust (**Amberlee**) (the **Acquisition**). A related land sale contract provides for Tasman Tourism Property Pty Ltd as trustee for the Tasman Tourism Property Trust to acquire the land at 306 Jetty Road, Rosebud, Victoria. The assets to be acquired include goodwill, permits, plant and equipment, records, intellectual property rights and the vendor’s interest in the relevant park lease.

Tasman Tourism is an entity within the Tasman Holiday Parks corporate group (**THP**), being the group of companies and unit trusts which own, develop and operate holiday parks in Australia and New Zealand. THP operates 38 holiday parks in Australia.

THP is managed by Tasman Capital, a mid-market focused Australian private equity firm with investments across Australia and New Zealand. Tasman Capital does not have any investments in holiday park operators, other than THP.

The vendor is Amberlee Family Holidays Pty Ltd as trustee for Amberlee Family Trust. Amberlee operates a holiday park business at 306 Jetty Road, Rosebud, Victoria 3939, under the trading name "Amberlee Holiday Homes & Accommodation", and a separate residential park business under the trading name "Woodlands Estate" at the same location. The Amberlee Holiday Homes & Accommodation business includes the sale of permanent holiday accommodation, cabins and caravans, as well as a small number of short-term tourist sites and related holiday park facilities. Woodlands Estate is a residential/land-lease community for customers aged over 55, at the same location.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between THP (and its
connected entities) and Amberlee in the supply of holiday
park accommodation in the Mornington Peninsula region of
Victoria, and a very small overlap in Victoria
b. there is no horizontal overlap between Tasman Capital (and
its portfolio companies) and Amberlee in the supply of
residential land lease communities in the Mornington
Peninsula region, and a very small overlap in Victoria
c. there are alternative suppliers of holiday parks and
residential land lease communities in the Mornington
Peninsula region and in Victoria more broadly.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
